research_objective:
Focus group guide exploring how to formulate a brief, accessible,
self-administered online mindfulness intervention for individuals
interested in meditation but constrained by limited time and financial
resources and seeking stress relief. The proposed intervention is
intended to be fully online, use audio tracks for mindfulness exercises,
and require a shorter time commitment than traditional 8-week
Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) courses.
topic_domain: Self-administered online mindfulness intervention, stress reduction, and sham meditation control
participant_collective_identity: Certified mindfulness instructors with between 7 and 15 years of professional experience
moderator_knowledge_brief:
Explore how to design an online, self-administered mindfulness
intervention for the general population experiencing medium to high
stress levels while facing time and financial constraints. The discussion
should cover adaptation from traditional mindfulness or MBSR-based
approaches, key mindfulness components, online delivery, session
frequency and duration, audio track structure, participant motivation,
and the design of a credible sham meditation control condition.

Participants are certified mindfulness instructors with between 7 and 15
years of professional experience.

The moderator should keep the discussion exploratory and non-leading. Use
the scripted questions as the spine of the session, but listen actively and
briefly synthesize participants' contributions when helpful to validate
understanding, connect related points, or transition to the next topic. Do
not turn participant-generated ideas into pre-planned probes unless those
ideas emerge naturally during the live discussion.

discussion_guide.scripted_question:
Thank you very much for taking the time to participate in this focus
group. Today we will discuss how to create an effective
self-administered mindfulness intervention for people who are facing
time and financial constraints and are seeking stress relief. The idea
is to design an intervention that is practical, impactful, accessible,
and suitable for people experiencing medium to high levels of stress.

We will discuss key components for stress reduction, as well as the
duration and frequency of the audio mindfulness tracks that may be part
of this intervention. If we have time, we will also discuss how to
create a balanced control group for the research that matches the
mindfulness intervention.

Please feel free to share your thoughts openly. There are no right or
wrong answers. You may not need to answer every question; please answer
the questions you feel able to respond to. I will moderate the session,
but I will not provide my own answers to these questions.

discussion_guide.section_label: Online adaptation and key mindfulness components
discussion_guide.section_purpose: Section 1: Online adaptation and key mindfulness components
discussion_guide.scripted_question:
1. How can we effectively adapt traditional mindfulness practices from
MBSR to an online format while ensuring their efficacy? Note that it
does not have to be necessarily an adapted version of MBSR; it must be
an intervention that can be self-administered and is functional to
reduce stress levels of participants.

2. Can we design a mindfulness protocol centered solely on key
mindfulness components, for example acceptance, to maximize impact on
stress regulation? Which components should take precedence?

3. What elements are crucial for the success of an online mindfulness
training if we consider stress reduction as the main outcome of the
intervention?
suggested_probes: Would you keep the whole structure of a traditional MBSR protocol in a condensed form, or would you select only some contents?

discussion_guide.scripted_question:
1. What is the optimal duration and frequency for each online
mindfulness session to balance effectiveness and practicality for our
target audience of stressed individuals with time constraints?

2. How should each mindfulness track be structured? Consider an
introductory segment, for example providing an overview of mindfulness
and/or presenting an attitude like nonjudging, followed by a
mindfulness exercise.

3. How can we motivate participants to integrate mindfulness into their
daily routines, considering their time and resource constraints?
suggested_probes: Should participants meditate every day, or would it be better to practise three times a week?
Would the track be entirely the mindfulness exercise, or would it also include a psychoeducational part at the beginning?

discussion_guide.section_purpose: Section 3: Control group and sham meditation
discussion_guide.scripted_question:
To establish a balanced control group, that is, a sham meditation
condition, it is necessary to create a control condition where
individuals believe they are engaging in meditation, yet the components
of mindfulness are absent.

Developing a sham meditation track involves creating an audio session
that mimics the appearance of a genuine mindfulness exercise. It should
have a comparable word count and comparable instructions to maintain
balance with the mindfulness condition, while strategically omitting key
mindfulness elements. This sham meditation should convincingly simulate
the meditation experience, allowing for a rigorous comparative analysis.

How would you structure this sham meditation intervention?

Thank you very much for participating today. Before we finish, is
there anything else you would like to add about the design of the
mindfulness intervention, the audio tracks, or the control condition?
